facts.text: It is Bhutan’s principal school for teaching the country’s traditional arts and crafts.
The institute teaches the thirteen traditional arts and crafts known in Bhutanese as Zorig Chusum.
Its curriculum includes disciplines such as painting, woodcarving, sculpture, embroidery, weaving and metalwork.
The school was established in 1971 to preserve and transmit Bhutan’s traditional artistic skills.
It is located in Thimphu, Bhutan’s capital, in the western part of the country.
Kuang Si Waterfall is a multi-tiered waterfall system on the Kuang Si River.
The main cascade falls over limestone terraces from a height of about 50 metres.
The waterfall forms a series of naturally calcified, blue-green pools below the main drop.
It lies in a forested limestone landscape in Luang Prabang Province, southwest of Luang Prabang.
